sentences.text: Shri Chandra Prakash Purohit, learned counsel for the a  Shri Mayank Upadhyay, learned counsel for the responden  ORDER Heard on I.A. No.8086/2023, which is an application for condonation of delay.
There is a delay of 95 days in fling the present appeal.
For the reasons stated in the application, I.A. No.8086/2023 is allowed and the delay in filing the appeal is condoned.
2. The appellants have filed this appeal being aggrieved by the award dated 04.03.2023 passed passed in MACC No.1643/2021 challenging the quantum of compensation.
3. The liability of the insurance company is not under dispute.

4. The short facts of the case are that on 10.05.2020, the deceased Bhagwan Patidar was going by his motorcycle towards his agricultural field, when he reached near village-Harsola Datoda Road the rider of motorcycle of MP09-VS- 8031 came driving the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed into the motorcycle of Bhagwan because of which he sustained grievous injuries, he was admitted in Mewada Hospital, Kishan Ganj, Mhow and thereafter he was taken to Apolo Rajshree Hospital where during treatment he died on 12.05.2020.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29255 2 MA-5835-2023 5.
The claimants filed a claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Bhagwan.
The claims tribunal after considering the evidence brought on record awarded compensation of Rs.11,79,700/- out of which an amount of Rs.8,71,200/- was for loss of dependency.

1 6.

Learned counsel for the appellants refers paragraph Nos.21 and 22 of the impugned award and points out that the deceased was working as driver in Umiya Girls School, Rau and was earning Rs.9973/- per month, his income was proved by the witness transport in-charge Jaynarayan Patidar PW-3 who has clearly deposed about the salary of the deceased at Rs.9973/- per month for which salary certificate Ex.P-36 was also brought on record.
The salary attendance register Ex.P-44 was also placed on record which certifies the attendance from February, 2020 to May, 2020.
Apart from this, bank statement Ex.P-45 was also placed on record.

The claims tribunal although believed the claim of income of the deceased, however, while calculating his income an amount of Rs.973/- was deducted from the same in view of the statutory deductions and his income was taken as Rs.9000/-
per month.

Learned counsel further submits that there is no justification for reducing the income of the deceased to Rs.9000/- from Rs.9973/- once the documents were duly placed on record and same were not discarded by the claims tribunal.
He thus prays for enhancement of compensation by correction in the income of the deceased.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/insurance company submits that the claims tribunal has correctly assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.9000/- per month.

He points out that after deductions the deceased received Rs.9000/- per month which has duly been considered by the claims tribunal in para 22 and what the deceased was receiving has been taken as his income,
hence, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29255 3 MA-5835-2023 he supports the findings of the award and prays for dismissal of the appeal.
8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9.

From perusal of Ex.P36 and Ex.P-42 to Ex.P-45 it is clear that the salary of the deceased was Rs.9973/- per month though it is clear that the deceased was receiving Rs.9000/- per month after deductions, however, the statutory deductions cannot be reduced while assessing the income of the deceased.
The statutory deductions were also the part of the income of the deceased, thus, the entire salary of the deceased should be taken into consideration.

As such, the income of the deceased is taken as Rs.9973/- per month and after modification in the income, the total compensation would now come to Rs.9,65,382/- in the head of loss of dependency and after deducting already awarded amount of Rs.8,71,200/- under this head the enhanced amount of Rs.94,182/- is required to be paid to the appellants with interest @6% per annum from the date of application before the claims tribunal.
This enhanced amount shall be paid over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal.
10. With the aforesaid, the appeal stands disposed of.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
